sn36.3:1.1: “Feeling” (_vedanā_) is the affective or hedonic tone of experience. Each sense can trigger a response of pleasure, pain, or neither-pleasure-nor-pain. It is from the root _vid_ (“know”), and is close in meaning to “experience”. For history, see note at [sn12.1:2.8]().
sn36.3:1.4: The feelings themselves are inherent to the functioning of the mind, so they remain so long as the mind remains. But how we respond to feelings is conditioned by underlying tendencies, which can be abandoned.
